analysis.title: Initial Jobless Claims Were Little Changed
key_insights: Initial jobless claims were 203,000 in the week ending November 14, slightly above PNC's forecast of 198,000 and down 19,000 from the same week a year earlier.
The four-week moving average of initial claims rose slightly but has stayed below 200,000 for seven consecutive weeks. It is down 27,000 from the same week in 2025.
Continuing claims rose by 70,000 to 1.763 million in the week ending November 7. They are down 186,000 from a year earlier.
The four-week moving average of continuing claims is 12.1% below its level in the same week last year.
The insured unemployment rate was 1.1% in the week ending November 7, unchanged for 11 weeks and down from 1.3% a year earlier.

The four-week average of initial claims was little changed during the November 12 survey reference week for nonfarm payrolls. PNC reads this as limited downside risk to November payroll growth, with job gains broadly in line with the recent trend.
PNC says continued low claims indicate layoffs remain low and the labor market remains healthy.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Claims are near 200,000, consistent with low layoffs.
The actual print came in 5,000 above PNC's forecast.
